class.name: RenderingEngine4D
class.brief_description: Abstract base class for 4D rendering engines.
class.description: RenderingEngine4D provides an interface for implementing 4D renderers. It is an abstract base class, so it must be extended to be used. Rendering engines must be registered with [RenderingServer4D] to be used. In comparison to Godot's rendering architecture, this is the 4D equivalent of RendererScene (not exposed). Godot's RendererScene is named "scene" to distinguish 3D scene rendering from 2D canvas rendering, but for 4D we do not need to distinguish from canvas rendering, and so we call this "rendering engine" for naming parity with physics engines. [b]Note:[/b] All of the properties in this class will be overwritten by [RenderingServer4D] each frame. Modifying them will have no external effect.

method.name: _cleanup_for_viewport
method.description: Callback method to clean up the rendering engine for a viewport. This method is called by [RenderingServer4D] once per viewport when it tries to render a frame with a different rendering engine than the one that was previously set up for that viewport. This is called before [method _setup_for_viewport] is called for the new rendering engine for that viewport.

method.name: _get_friendly_name
method.description: Callback method that should return the unique friendly name of the rendering engine. This is used by [RenderingServer4D] to identify the rendering engine for a viewport, and is displayed in the editor. It should be a short, human-readable name that describes the rendering engine. This MUST be unique across all registered rendering engines.

method.name: _prefers_wireframe_meshes
method.description: Callback method to determine if the rendering engine prefers meshes to be wireframe. Used to decide which type of optimized meshes should be supplied in the scene, such as for editor gizmos: [WireMesh4D] if [code]true[/code], or [TetraMesh4D] if [code]false[/code]. Non-optimized [PolyMesh4D] meshes are slower, but will display optimally in both wireframe and non-wireframe rendering engines.

method.name: _render_frame
method.description: Callback method to render a frame. This method is called by [RenderingServer4D] every frame. The current camera, all meshes, and their transforms are passed in.

method.name: _setup_for_viewport
method.description: Callback method to set up the rendering engine for a viewport. This method is called by [RenderingServer4D] once per viewport before calling [method _render_frame] for the first time for that viewport. In this function, only [member viewport] may be accessed. All other properties must not be accessed inside this function as they may contain stale data from other viewports or be null/empty.

method.name: _supports_lighting
method.description: Callback method to determine if the rendering engine supports lighting. Used by the editor to display lighting options when using this rendering engine.

method.name: get_camera
method.description: Returns the [Camera4D] node currently being rendered by the rendering engine. This will be set by [RenderingServer4D] before calling [method _render_frame].

method.name: get_friendly_name
method.description: Returns the unique friendly name of the rendering engine. This is used by [RenderingServer4D] to identify the rendering engine for a viewport, and is displayed in the editor. It should be a short, human-readable name that describes the rendering engine. This MUST be unique across all registered rendering engines.

method.name: get_mesh_instance_object_ids
method.description: Returns an array of ObjectIDs (packed in a [PackedInt64Array]) of visible [MeshInstance4D] nodes to be rendered by the rendering engine. This will be set by [RenderingServer4D] before calling [method _render_frame]. The size of this array will match the size of the [member mesh_relative_basises] and [member mesh_relative_positions] arrays, and each index of each array will correspond to the mesh at that index. To convert the ObjectIDs to [MeshInstance4D] nodes, in GDScript use [method @GlobalScope.instance_from_id], or in C++ use [code]ObjectDB::get_instance((ObjectID)arr[index])[/code], or preferably as separate statements use [code]const ObjectID oid = (ObjectID)arr[index]; ObjectDB::get_instance(oid)[/code] (an explicit cast to [code]ObjectID[/code] is required in C++).

method.name: get_mesh_relative_basises
method.description: Returns the basis part of the mesh transform relative to the camera. This will be set by [RenderingServer4D] before calling [method _render_frame]. The size of this array will match the size of the [member mesh_instances] and [member mesh_relative_positions] arrays, and each index of each array will correspond to the mesh at that index.

method.name: get_mesh_relative_positions
method.description: Returns the position part of the mesh transform relative to the camera. This will be set by [RenderingServer4D] before calling [method _render_frame]. The size of this array will match the size of the [member mesh_instances] and [member mesh_relative_basises] arrays, and each index of each array will correspond to the mesh at that index.

method.name: get_viewport
method.description: Returns the [Viewport] that the rendering engine is rendering to. This will be set by [RenderingServer4D] before calling [method _setup_for_viewport].

method.name: prefers_wireframe_meshes
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the rendering engine prefers meshes to be wireframe. Used to decide which type of optimized meshes should be supplied in the scene, such as for editor gizmos: [WireMesh4D] if [code]true[/code], or [TetraMesh4D] if [code]false[/code]. Non-optimized [PolyMesh4D] meshes are slower, but will display optimally in both wireframe and non-wireframe rendering engines.

method.name: supports_lighting
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the rendering engine supports lighting. Used by the editor to display lighting options when using this rendering engine.
